title: Plan a production day, sell safely, earn your certificate

say: Plan a production day, sell safely, and earn your certificate.
This is the video for module four of Basic Baking and Snacks Production.
The secret of a calm production day is planning backwards from the delivery time. Write the time, the place, and how long the journey takes.

panel.heading: Start from the delivery time
items: What you can do the day before

say: Allow time for cooling and packing. Hot food must cool before you close boxes.

panel.heading: Start from the delivery time
items: What you can do the day before

say: Count your oven rounds or frying batches, and how long each takes.

panel.heading: Start from the delivery time
items: What you can do the day before

say: Add preparation time: weighing, mixing, rising, filling and shaping.

panel.heading: Start from the delivery time
items: What you can do the day before

say: And move safe jobs to the day before, like shopping, dry weighing, and cooking and chilling the filling.

panel.heading: Start from the delivery time
items: What you can do the day before

say: For example, Halima in Abuja must deliver 50 meat pies and 100 puff-puff at 10:30 am on Saturday. On Friday she shops, checks her gas level, and cooks the filling. She cools it and refrigerates it within 2 hours, and weighs dry ingredients into labelled bags.

panel.heading: 50 meat pies and 100 puff-puff
items: Day before: shop, check gas, cook filling

say: Saturday at 5:30, she makes the pastry, so it is chilled by 6:15.

panel.heading: 50 meat pies and 100 puff-puff
items: Day before: shop, check gas, cook filling

say: Her oven bakes 16 pies per round, so she needs 4 rounds, about 2 hours. She starts at 6:30. At 7:30 she mixes the puff-puff batter, which needs about an hour to rise.

panel.heading: 50 meat pies and 100 puff-puff
items: Day before: shop, check gas, cook filling

say: From 8:30 she fries the puff-puff while the last pies cool.

panel.heading: 50 meat pies and 100 puff-puff
items: Day before: shop, check gas, cook filling

say: At 9:30 she packs and labels.

panel.heading: 50 meat pies and 100 puff-puff
items: Day before: shop, check gas, cook filling

say: She leaves at 10:00 and delivers on time, with 5 spare pies for quality checks. Keep children out of the kitchen while oil is hot, and do not leave meat pies in a hot car.

panel.heading: 50 meat pies and 100 puff-puff
items: Day before: shop, check gas, cook filling
panel.rule: Cook, cool and refrigerate filling within 2 hours

say: On WhatsApp Business, add a catalogue with real photos at real size, dated prices and allergens. Confirm every order in writing.

say: For schools and offices, bring a sample tray. For example, Chioma in Owerri takes 10 meat pies and 20 puff-puff to a school administrator, and wins a two-week trial that becomes a steady order.

say: For shops, show your labelled product and wholesale price list, and get each delivery signed. Limit credit. Unpaid credit is one of the fastest ways to run out of money.

say: Fake transfer alerts and fake screenshots are common. Never release goods because of an SMS or screenshot alone. Open your own bank or mobile money app and confirm the money is in your balance.

Never share your PIN, password or one-time code, even with someone who says they are from your bank. For big event orders, ask for a deposit, for example 50%, before you buy ingredients. And keep business money in a separate account.

panel.heading: Payment safety
items: Never release goods on an SMS or screenshot
Never share your PIN or one-time code
Deposit for big orders, for example 50%

say: Every week, track units sold, waste, profit and repeat customers. For example, in week one, 200 pieces are made and 176 sold.
200 minus 176 leaves 24 not sold or rejected.
24 divided by 200 is 0.12.
Multiply by 100, and waste is 12%. By week three in the example, waste falls to 5% and repeat customers rise to 12. That shows quality and planning are improving.

panel.heading: Working out waste %
panel.rule: Falling waste and rising repeat customers mean progress

say: Your portfolio proves real practice. Two recipes in grams, clear dated photos, batch records, a costing sheet, a label with allergens, tasting scores and an honest reflection. Include problems and how you fixed them.
Then a 90-day plan, with products, customers and a few numbers. To earn the certificate, complete the project and score at least 70% in the final quiz.
Your practice: plan and run an order of at least 30 pieces, build your sales kit, approach one school, office or shop, and write your reflection and 90-day plan.
Now continue with the lessons below.
